page: Amazon Web Services x8i.large is a memory-optimized cloud virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with two vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading on an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz. The CPU incorporates an extensive 480 MB L3 cache along with advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. System memory consists of 32 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, delivering an extreme memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. The instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached volumes, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated GPU acceleration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance alongside constrained multi-core throughput dictated by the 1-core, 2-thread physical footprint. In synthetic evaluation, the instance achieved a Geekbench single-core score of 2154.0, ranking in the upper 25 percent of tested machines, complemented by strong single-threaded gzip compression of 34.34 GB/s and bzip3 decompression of 14.36 GB/s. In contrast, multi-threaded metrics such as PassMark CPU (4078.61), multi-core Geekbench (2719.0), and stress-ng multi-core scores land in the lower quartiles. Memory bandwidth yields 20.29 GB/s on large-block reads and 16.61 GB/s on writes, with redis SET performance logging 3.82 million operations per second.

Given its heavy memory allocation relative to compute capability, the x8i.large is cost-efficient primarily for memory-bound applications that require substantial working sets without necessitating broad multi-core processing power. It is well-suited for small in-memory caches, light database workloads, memory-intensive batch extract-transform-load (ETL) processing, and single-threaded analytics tasks where memory density per vCPU is paramount.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.large is a memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-dense workloads requiring modest compute capacity. Powered by the AWS Nitro System, the instance features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, allocating two vCPUs across a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It is paired with 32 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz, providing a generous 16 GB of RAM per vCPU, supported by a 480 MB L3 cache and AMX acceleration. The instance does not bundle local disk storage and connects at a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing exhibits strong single-core CPU and compression metrics alongside lower aggregate multi-core throughput. Consequently, the x8i.large provides balanced cost efficiency for lightweight relational databases, in-memory key-value caching, and memory-bound background tasks.
